coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: Easy 6–8 miles, Z2 (140–150 bpm), rolling terrain if possible—no hard efforts. You're 21 days out and in taper; your resting HR is 8 bpm above baseline (74 vs. 66.5 avg), which signals incomplete recovery from this week's 24.5-mile block. Yesterday's 5.12-mile run at 144 avg HR was solid, but Friday in taper is a shakeout day, not a workout day. Keep it conversational, sub-threshold, and use it to prime your legs for Saturday's long run without digging into glycogen or nervous system reserves.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: You're traveling for work and slept 8.3h with 70% efficiency—that's a 90-minute net sleep loss from your 30-day average. Nail breakfast: 60–80g carbs + 25g protein within 90 minutes of waking. During today's easy run, drink to thirst only (you're not depleting at Z2). Post-run, prioritize a full recovery meal within 30 minutes: 1g carbs per kg bodyweight + 0.25g protein per kg. Your moderate recovery score (46/100) means your glycogen and mineral status matter more than usual right now—don't skimp on carbs or sodium this week.

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep efficiency dropped to 70%—likely travel-related stress or time zone drift. Tonight, aim for 8.5–9 hours in a cool, dark room; your baseline is 8.2h, so you're chasing an extra 20–30 minutes to offset this week's training load. Your elevated resting HR (74) and moderate recovery score both point to incomplete parasympathetic reset. Skip ice baths and high-intensity mobility; do 10 minutes of easy foam rolling and 15 minutes of supine breathing work instead. If you're still traveling, prioritize sleep over meetings tomorrow morning if possible.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're 3 weeks out and have logged serious volume; the taper is now where fitness becomes confidence. Your recent runs show solid aerobic base (9.01mi at 115 bpm, 623 ft vert at 144 bpm)—you're ready for the alpine demands of Kranjska Gora. This week, let go of the urge to 'test' fitness; taper doubt is real, but it's a liar. Your job now is to arrive rested, fueled, and sharp. Use today's easy run as a mental reset: flow state, rhythm, gratitude for the base you've built. Saturday's long run will be your final dress rehearsal—trust the training.
